---
title: "Airway"
sidebarTitle: "Overview"
description: "Oxygen's ELT engine, which extracts data from external systems and loads it into your warehouse"
---

**Airway** is Oxygen's ELT engine. It extracts data from external systems
such as point-of-sale platforms, accounting tools, public datasets, and other
databases, and loads it into your warehouse, usually
[Airhouse](/guide/build/data-infrastructure/airhouse), where
[Airform](/guide/build/data-infrastructure/airform) and the
[semantic model](/guide/build/semantic-model/simple-model) take over. Every
pipeline comes down to three things:

- A **pipeline file** in your workspace that declares what to extract, from
  where, and where to load it.
- A **run**, which is queued, extracts only what changed, and loads it into
  your warehouse.
- A **cursor**, saved per workspace, which records how far the last run got
  so that the next run, or a retry, resumes from there.

## Why incremental, one run at a time

Re-pulling a source's full history on every run is slow, costs API quota, and
makes a failure expensive, because a retry starts again from the beginning.
Running two loads of the same pipeline at once is worse: they race on the
same tables and can skip or double-load rows.

Airway avoids both. Each pipeline keeps a cursor, so a run extracts only what
changed since the last one, and a retry resumes from that cursor rather than
from scratch. Only one run of a pipeline is active per workspace at a time, so
the cursor has a single writer. The cursor only advances after a load
commits, so a failure can make the next run re-read a window, but never
skip one.

## The pipeline file

Each pipeline is a version-controlled `.airway.yml` file in your workspace,
declaring a source, a destination, and optionally which of the source's
resources to load:

```yaml
# pipelines/quickbooks_financials.airway.yml
name: quickbooks_financials
source:
  kind: quickbooks
  config:
    client_id: <client-id>
    client_secret_var: QB_CLIENT_SECRET   # a secret key, never a value
    refresh_token_var: QB_REFRESH_TOKEN
    realm_id: "<realm-id>"
destination:
  database: warehouse                      # a database from config.yml
  dataset_name: quickbooks_financials
concurrency: 2
```

The `.airway.yml` extension is required, because the workspace only picks up
files with that exact suffix; a pipeline saved as plain `.yml` is silently
ignored. Credentials never appear in the file: a key ending in `_var` names a
secret in the workspace's secret manager, and Oxygen substitutes its value at
run time. The [pipeline reference](/guide/build/data-infrastructure/airway/pipelines)
lists every key and every supported source.

## How a run works

- **Queue.** Only one run of a given pipeline is active per workspace. A run
  submitted while another is busy waits for it, and repeated submissions join
  the run already queued, so ten clicks of **Run now** produce one run.
- **Extract.** The run reads only what changed since the cursor, extracting
  the source's resources in parallel up to the pipeline's `concurrency`.
- **Load.** Rows are loaded into the destination, and the cursor advances once
  the load has committed. New tables and columns are added automatically, but
  a column is never dropped or narrowed in place, so a pipeline sitting on a
  wrong schema needs an explicit **Reset schema**, which drops its destination
  tables and cursor so that the next run starts fresh.
- **Finish.** A run ends as `completed`, `completed_with_errors`, or `failed`.
  A run that loads some resources but fails on others finishes as
  `completed_with_errors` rather than as a failure, so alerting should watch
  for both.

## Triggers

Pipelines can run on their own with **Run now**, from a schedule, or as a step
in an [automation](/guide/build/automations/task-types#type-airway), where the
step finishes only once the load has committed, so that the tasks after it
read fully loaded tables.

## Destinations

Pipelines load into a database declared in `config.yml`. In practice this is
almost always an [Airhouse](/guide/build/data-infrastructure/airhouse)
database, which mints credentials at run time so the pipeline never holds a
warehouse password. Postgres destinations are also supported.
